messages:
emily: Hi team! New joiner here. Running into a puzzling Postgres issue on my Windows laptop. Using Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend. Repo is on C:\Users\emily\code\redwood-sample and I did `docker compose up`. The db container crashes during init with errors like: "could not create directory \"pg_wal\": Permission denied" and "initdb: could not change permissions of directory \"/var/lib/postgresql/data\"". Any tips?

rafael: welcome! common WSL2 gotcha: bind-mounting host paths from the Windows filesystem (C:\) into Linux containers can hit permission and metadata mismatches because NTFS doesn't support Linux UID/GID semantics. Did you bind `./pgdata` to `/var/lib/postgresql/data`?

emily: yeah my compose has `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. I tried `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` inside WSL shell but the error persists.

kate: chown on the Windows-mounted path often no-ops because the underlying FS is NTFS. Two straightforward fixes: 1) move the project into the WSL filesystem (e.g., /home/emily/code/redwood-sample) and run compose there so the bind mount uses a native Linux FS, or 2) use a named Docker volume for Postgres (no host bind) so the engine manages permissions. For quick testing I usually do: `volumes: dbdata: {}` then `db: volumes: - dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in compose.

emily: moved the repo into \u007e/code inside WSL and restarted compose. Postgres starts now, migrations run. Nice! Quick follow-up: is there any reason to prefer named volume over WSL location?

rafael: named volume is simpler if you don't need host files visible. If you want to inspect db files from host, WSL2 FS is fine. Avoid persisting DB data on C:\host paths for dev. Also note Windows Defender can lock files if scanning; if you see `resource busy` errors, try excluding the project dir or use named volume.

emily: good to know. I also attempted to use redis unix sockets in dev because prod uses sockets, but discovered Docker Desktop on Windows doesn't support container-to-host unix sockets the same way. Should default to TCP for compose?

kate: yep, prefer TCP (redis://redis:6379) in compose dev stacks on Windows/WSL2. Unix sockets are flaky across host/VM boundaries.

emily: thanks — will add these notes to my onboarding checklist: 1) avoid binding Postgres data to Windows (C:) paths; use WSL FS or named volumes, 2) if stuck, move repo into WSL and rerun compose, 3) use TCP for Redis in compose on Windows. @rafael can we add a one-liner in the quickstart?

infra-bot: Dev-setup note created: "Windows + WSL2: avoid bind-mounting Postgres data to Windows (C:) drives; prefer WSL2 filesystem or Docker named volumes. Use TCP service hosts for Redis in compose. See https://go.redwood/dev-setup" (:book:)

emily: awesome, thanks everyone! Everything green now and I can continue the tutorial. :party:
